newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl meets Aznar in Germany for Euro talks.
newsitem.headline: Kohl meets Aznar in Germany for Euro talks.

text.p: Germany's Chancellor Helmut Kohl welcomed Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar to his homeland state Rhineland-Palatinate on Tuesday for informal talks on the single European currency.
The German leader welcomed Aznar at Frankfurt airport just hours after announcing he would receive Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi for dinner on Thursday evening in Bonn.

EU officials say Italy and Spain have relatively slim chances of qualifying on all the Maastricht Treaty requirements for economic and monetary union (EMU) despite their recent efforts to tighten fiscal controls to qualify.

The two meetings within the space of a week fired speculation Kohl might start to discuss a compromise allowing Spain and Italy to join the commmon European currency after it is launched in 1999 -- an idea favoured by some EU officials.

"If Spain and Italy were to join EMU in 1999 it could cause Kohl political problems at home," said senior analyst Thomas Meyer at Goldman Sachs, referring to Germans' reluctance to part with their beloved deutschemark for a weaker alternative.
"Germans will have to get used to idea that Spain and Italy want to pursue a hard monetary policy and it'll take time for them to accept this," Meyer told Reuters.

Holger Fahrinkrug, an analyst at UBS in Frankfurt, said a decision for Germany to join EMU could be challenged in the constitutional court if other EU members were allowed to join without fulfilling the criteria properly.

"Kohl is very pro-European and wants as much integration as possible. He will probably encourage them (Spain and Italy) to continue their efforts to introduce real, structural and not cosmetic changes," Fahrinkrug said.

"But if they fudge it and the treaty is broken, this would be a chance for anti-Europeans to challenge Germany's participation in EMU in the constitutional court," he said. "He may tell them they could join a little later."
Kohl showed Aznar around his old university town of Heidelberg and was later to entertain him for dinner at a castle in the picturesque village of Schwetzingen.
A German government spokesman accompanying Kohl was keen to stress that there were no fundamental differences between Kohl and his Spanish counterpart.
The leaders declined to comment on the content of their talks during a walkabout in Heidelberg.
Diplomatic sources in Bonn said Kohl's two meetings this week were the conclusion of a recent series of telephone conversations with his Italian and Spanish counterparts.
The leaders of the EU member states meet in December in Dublin to discuss Europe's future and which states are likely to qualify for the single currency due to be launched in 1999.
